title: Legislate the ban on non-compete clauses for low- and middle-income workers
action: Pass and commence the announced ban on non-compete clauses for workers below the high-income threshold, together with the bans on no-poach and wage-fixing agreements, and evaluate its effects on job mobility, wages and new businesses after a few years.
why: Non-compete clauses stop workers moving to the employer that values their skills most or starting a rival business, which holds back wages, new firms and the spread of know-how.

evidence.quote: The government announced reforms to worker restraints in the 2025-26 Budget. This includes banning: non-compete clauses for low- and middle-income workers wage-fixing agreements no-poach agreements.

evidence.source: National Competition Policy: modelling proposed reforms
evidence.quote: One is about limiting the unreasonable use of restraint of trade clauses (L1) - focusing on non-compete clauses, which impede the ability of workers to switch employers and start up rival businesses.

evidence.source: Working paper on options for reform of non-compete clauses in employment contracts
evidence.publisher: UK Department for Business and Trade
evidence.quote: There is broad consensus in the literature that they lower overall job mobility, particularly within the same industry and into roles that offer greater seniority.

progress.what: An exposure draft bill was released for consultation in September 2026, for commencement in 2027.
